thread:
sasha: Heads-up — we've got inconsistent client-side metadata shapes landing in policy headers from Py/TS/Go. Console routing dashboard shows split attribution and quotas are double-counted for some routes. Can we agree on a canonical header and a migration path?

mike: Ugh, saw that in the daily alerts. Quick example?

sasha: Example payloads observed in logs:
```
# TS client (current)
X-Redwood-Meta: route=chat.v1;cost_center=eng;session_id=abc123

# Py client (current)
X-Redwood-Meta: {"route":"chat.v1","team":"eng","sid":"abc123"}

# Go client (current)
X_Redwood_Meta: route=chat.v1|cc=eng|session:abc123
```
These are getting normalized differently in the policy proxy which then affects quota buckets and routing heuristics.

leon: Oof. Part of this came from earlier SDK convenience helpers — we tried to be permissive. But permissive -> ambiguous. Strong +1 for canonicalization.

anya: From console POV, current telemetry mapping assumes `cost_center` and `route` keys specifically. When it gets `team` or `cc` we map them heuristically and sometimes create a new pseudo-dimension. That's why dashboards show duplicates.

mike: Proposal: define a canonical header JSON shape: `X-Redwood-Context` with fields: `route`, `cost_center`, `session_id`, `env` and `client_version`. All SDKs must emit JSON. Keep old header names accepted for 3 months as a compatibility shim in the proxy. After that, reject noncanonical with 4xx and a telemetry counter.

leon: Sounds reasonable. Migration plan for SDKs:
- opt-in flag in next minor release to emit canonical JSON
- default emit in next major (with warning log for one minor)
- provide a small helper to translate legacy shapes -> canonical shape

leon: Example canonical header now:
```
X-Redwood-Context: {"route":"chat.v1","cost_center":"eng","session_id":"abc123","env":"prod","client_version":"py-0.23.1"}
```

anya: Console needs a clear signal for the rollout. Request: when we see legacy shapes during opt-in period, set a `context_migration_flag` in telemetry so UX can show % migrated by client version and route. Also add a console tile showing which customers still send legacy headers (privacy-safe hashes).

mike: Agree. Also add a migration mode in the policy proxy: 1) passthrough+telemetry, 2) normalize (proxy rewrites legacy -> canonical), 3) enforce (reject). Default deployment: start with passthrough+telemetry, then normalize, then enforce.

leon: Implementation notes for SDKs: minimal surface change. Add `emit_canonical_context=True` opt-in config and `redwood.context.normalize()` helper. We'll ship helpers for py/ts/go at the same time.

deploy-bot: canary deployed policy-proxy v2.14.0 with passthrough+telemetry mode enabled in us-west-2.

anya: Nice. One more ask: make the console migration tile filterable by `route` and `client_version` so product owners can prioritize enforcement for high-cost routes first.

mike: Will do. I'll draft the RFC for the canonical shape + proxy modes and include rollout timeline: opt-in period 6 weeks, normalization 4 weeks after opt-in, enforce 8 weeks after normalization. Feedback?

sasha: Timeline looks good. Two action items for SDK owners (leon): 1) helpers + opt-in in next minor, 2) deprecation warnings in logs when legacy keys detected. For platform: add telemetry counters and console tile work (anya). Thanks — let's avoid another quota attribution incident. :thumbsup:
